captive_summary: Proposed onshore LNG import terminal on the Taunton River in Fall River, MA (Hess LNG / Weaver's Cove Energy LLC), FERC docket underlying Docket Nos. 06-1203 et al. and 08-2440. Two First Circuit opinions describing the FERC-authorized project scope enumerate its facilities as 'a marine berth ..., an LNG storage tank, re-gasification facilities, and an LNG truck distribution facility' with no power-generation component named anywhere in either opinion (checked for 'generator', 'turbine', 'electric power', 'power plant', 'gas-fired', 'backup power', 'diesel generator' — all absent). Combined with the grid-access prior for a grid-connected New England (ISO-NE) onshore import terminal proposed in this era, this is a documented negative, not an inferred one. Hess withdrew the project entirely in 2015/2016 citing economics; it was never built.
confirmed_how: First Circuit, City of Fall River v. FERC, 507 F.3d 1 (2007): 'The facility, which would include a marine berth (requiring dredging of the harbor and waterways, including the Taunton River), an LNG storage tank, re-gasification facilities, and an LNG truck distribution facility...' — no generation facility listed. First Circuit, Weaver's Cove Energy, LLC v. Rhode Island CRMC (2009), describing the same FERC-authorized project, likewise contains no reference to on-site generation, turbines, or electric power anywhere in the opinion. Upstream/turnto10 news coverage (2015-16) confirms Hess abandoned the project before construction, citing unfavorable economics, i.e. it was never built beyond the FERC-authorized design these opinions describe.
